2_Introduction: The PCE for the device reached 15.61%, with a JSC of 20.77 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0118 V and a FF of 74.28%. Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 (1.73 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The deposition process involved a two-step spin sequence (1000 rpm/10 s and 5000 rpm/30 s) to achieve a controlled film thickness. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. Afterwards, the perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 2107.57 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.21, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI₂. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI₂.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppress phase segregation while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.73 eV—undergoes highly controlled crystallization governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent removal), where the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at 6 s before spin termination critically arrests nucleation kinetics, promoting uniform nucleation density and suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent evaporation and lattice reorganization without inducing halide disproportionation or volatile cation loss, yielding a compact, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with suppressed ion migration pathways and minimized deep-level traps at grain boundaries and surfaces. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition—where FA⁺ enhances structural stability, MA⁺ improves interfacial compatibility, and Cs⁺ rigidifies the lattice against thermal strain—synergistically mitigates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies, while the Br⁻ alloying (10% on X-site) subtly elevates the conduction band minimum and reduces lattice softness, collectively lowering non-radiative recombination centers. Critically, XRD characterization reveals only a weak residual PbI₂ peak at 12.65° (intensity = 2107.57 cts, FWHM = 0.21°), confirming near-complete conversion of the precursor into the desired perovskite phase with minimal secondary-phase impurities and low microstrain—as corroborated by the narrow FWHM, which reflects high crystallinity and reduced lattice disorder—thereby ensuring efficient charge extraction and diminished trap-assisted recombination across the bulk and interfaces. This structural and compositional fidelity directly manifests in superior optoelectronic quality, as evidenced by the high open-circuit voltage of 1.0118 V, short-circuit current density of 20.77 mA/cm², fill factor of 74.28%, and power conversion efficiency of 15.61%.
